title: Agent tab's first load runs as a background tab
notes: Found testing v2.58.0 (#377). A worker ran browser open on a data: fixture page and measured it 1.2 s later: visibilityState visible, but first-contentful-paint null and rAF 2 per second; timers ran at 100. After a browser go on the same tab it measured fcp 76 ms and rAF 145. So a new tab loads its page before its view is moved into the one-pixel held placement (viewBounds, browser-decision-9): makeView in src/main/browser/browser-views.ts calls loadURL while the view is setVisible(false) at lastBounds, and the open action's keep() places it only afterwards. An agent that opens a page and measures it straight away, the new-crm case, still gets no paint metrics. Fix: a tab opened for a pane is placed in its held spot (visible, one pixel in the window) before its first load starts, without taking the keyboard (browser-rule-4). Test the placement decision, and in a dev build check the fixture: fcp recorded and rAF about 60/s on the first load. The fixture is /tmp/dashboard-test/page.html (url.txt holds its data: URL, measure.js the eval). Never restart the running app.

comments.body: Stopped before a pull request: the diagnosis does not reproduce. I built this branch (v2.58.0) as a throwaway copy (its own HOME and --user-data-dir, through the scripts/performance demo launcher) and ran the card's fixture from a worker pane: browser open, sleep 1.2, eval measure.js, then browser go and measure again. The old order (makeView loads before keep places the view) already paints on the first load. Headless weston: first load fcp 84 ms, rAF 62; after go fcp 64, rAF 61. Real Wayland display: first load fcp 208, rAF 63; after go fcp 64, rAF 62. Real display with the browser screen shown first and a tab already open: first load fcp 92, rAF 61. With the fix (the open action calls a new start port after keep), headless gave first load fcp 156, rAF 59, so no difference either way. Whatever gave fcp null and rAF 2/s in the installed app, it is not the load starting before placement. What differs from my runs and may matter: the installed app's uptime and open tabs, the 144 Hz display (rAF 145 there), the window or workspace state at the time, and which project page was on screen. The fix is committed on this branch (b905d70c: tabs.ts, browser-ports.ts, browser-views.ts, a test in tabs.test.ts) but not pushed. It is harmless and right by construction, but it fixes nothing I can measure. Next step: reproduce in the installed app with the window state written down, then diagnose again.
